about.title: Hidden Hills Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Hidden Hills is a small, gated equestrian community, but that doesn't mean its private and connecting roads are free of collisions. Streets like Jed Smith Road, El Dorado Meadow Road, Eldorado Meadow Road, and Lewis and Clark Road see regular local traffic, horseback riders, and pedestrians sharing tight lanes, and crash reports here tend to cluster on Tuesday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. when residents are commuting home. Whether you were driving, a passenger, or walking near one of these corridors, sorting out fault and insurance coverage can be confusing, especially in a community where roads may be privately maintained. LawProactive connects injured Hidden Hills residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the crash, deal with insurance adjusters, and explain your options under California law. This is a free connection service, not a law firm, and any attorney you're matched with works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Dealing With the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity's road maintenance was involved. An attorney can help identify which deadline applies to your situation before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover damages, just reduced by your share of fault. Insurers often try to inflate your percentage of blame, which is why having someone review the evidence on your behalf matters.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit the emotional distress and pain-and-suffering damages you may seek in a standard car accident claim. An attorney can help make sure those non-economic losses are properly documented and not minimized during negotiations.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since insurers often use those statements to shift blame or minimize your claim. Anything you say can be reviewed later out of context. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to share and when.

items.question: What if my accident happened on a private road in Hidden Hills?
items.answer: Many roads in Hidden Hills are privately maintained by the community association rather than a public agency, which can affect who's responsible for hazards like poor lighting or unrepaired surfaces. This distinction matters for both liability and filing deadlines. An attorney can help sort out whether a private entity, a driver, or both may share responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in California?
items.answer: Generally, California law gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a county road department, may be involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's important to act quickly. Preserving evidence like photos, witness contacts, and vehicle damage early on also strengthens your position.
